title: Pelican Stores
subtitle: Data visualization project.
html:
View full presentation · Canva ↗

Turning retail transactions into comparable questions

This Tableau visualization project uses 100 retail transactions from the Pelican Stores case to examine customer type, payment method, items purchased, net sales, and demographics. It asks who buys, how customer behavior differs, and which segments deserve closer attention.

Moving from distributions to multidimensional comparisons

The analysis begins with payment methods and age distributions, then compares promotional and regular customers by items purchased and net sales. A heatmap combines age, marital status, and customer type to compare average sales across segments.

A chart of items purchased against net sales explores how basket size relates to revenue. Each visualization answers a distinct question while contributing to a broader view of customer behavior.

Main observations in the presentation

Within the sample, promotional customers buy more items on average but vary more widely, while regular customers show more consistent net sales. The presentation identifies ages 26–45 as the main customer group and reports a positive relationship between items purchased and net sales.

These observations support further questions about segmentation and promotions, including how additional purchases compare with revenue stability rather than judging a campaign by total sales alone.

Why the project matters

Different ways of grouping the same transactions can lead to different business judgments. The project demonstrates chart selection, cross-segment comparison, and translation of observations into marketing questions. The 100-transaction case describes a sample; it does not establish market-wide behavior or prove that a promotion caused an outcome.

Case-data analysis; observations are drawn from the presentation and are not presented as verified company-wide results.
